summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles around 2002. He held posts at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, Oberlin College, and taught at UCSB, UIUC, and the University of Hawaii.
David Faure is a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong from around 1966 to 1969 and at Princeton University from around 1970 to 1976.

David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. In roughly 2008, he became associate professor and department chair at Linfield University.
David Friedman was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. From around 1950 to 1970, he served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and as a professor at the University of London.

David Germano is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison between 1984 and 1992, and became an associate professor at the University of Virginia around 1992.
David Gonsalez is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Kali Charan Bahl, and held posts at Chicago, the University of Virginia (~1986–1996), and UC Santa Barbara (~1996–2019).

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso and David Karma Choephel, and completed work supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes before taking a post at the University of Vienna around 2012.

David J. Kalupahana was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman, later holding posts at the University of Ceylon (~1959–1972) and the University of Hawaii (~1972–2000).

David Jones is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Hawaii around 1996. He has served as director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies and professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia.

David K. Wyatt was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He held academic posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell University (~1969–2002).

David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago between 2011 and 2019 under Dan Arnold, and later held a post at Smith College.

David Kinsley was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago. From 1969 to 2000, he held a post at McMaster University.

David Kopf was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 1960 to 1964 and held a post at the University of Minnesota from around 1967 to 2004.
David L. Gosling is an Indology and religious studies scholar who held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and held a post at the University of Cambridge.

David L. Haberman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder from around 1972 to 1976. He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (~1993).

David L. McMahan is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont. In roughly 1999, he became assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Franklin & Marshall College.

David L. Snellgrove was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Southampton, Queens' College, and the University of Cambridge. He served as a professor at SOAS and the University of London from 1950 to 1982.

David Ludden is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia (~1979–1981), the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–2007), and New York University (~2007).

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, before joining the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee around 2012.
